title: CCTV switches: same models and ports as the Server Inventory switches
items: 📹 on the Racks tab now adds the CCTV switches as Cisco C9200L-48P-4X-E (48 ports GE 1/0/1–48 + 4 uplinks T 1/1/1–4, like the IT switches) and WS-C3560CX-12PD-S (12 ports + 2 uplinks GE 1/0/13–14, like the card-reader switches); the MR-01 CCTV switches without a model in their label as C9200L-48P.

CCTV switches already added with the first layout are corrected by the same button ("Correct n CCTV switches"): model set, missing ports added, empty extra ports removed, and a used uplink with the old name renamed (TE 1/1/1 → T 1/1/1) together with its far end — nothing written on a port is lost.

title: Network map: CCTV switches added from the racks
items: Racks tab (admins): 📹 Add CCTV switches to the map turns the CCTV switches that were only labels in the racks (SR-02/CCTV-ASW-03(9200) … SR-31/CCTV-ASW-24(3560), MR-01/CCTV-ASW-01/02, the CCTV distribution switches MR-02/CCTV-DSW-01 and MR-03/CCTV-DSW-02) into real devices of the map, linked to their rack slot, with ports: Catalyst 9200 = 24 + 4 uplinks, 3560CX = 14, distribution switches none (add their ports by hand). Preview first; the button disappears once done.

They show in the device list, the Topology, the CCTV / HARICI KABIN popups of the site plan ("Plugged into …") and in the OT view. Their cameras appear as soon as the ports are filled (port edit, OT device list or 🔌 Switch ports); set the uplink port to the CCTV distribution switch to connect them on the Topology.

title: Site plan: click a Kabin to see and edit everything plugged into it
items: Drawings → Site — outdoor cabinets & fibre routes (and the other plans): click a cabinet (IT KABIN, HARICI KABIN …) and its popup now lists, per switch in that cabinet, every device plugged into it — port number, icon, name, OT devices in orange. Click a device to open its port right on top of the plan and edit it (name, VLAN, patch, note …); the popup refreshes after saving. IT editors can edit any port, OT editors the end-device ports of their switches (ports to network devices stay IT's).
The plugged-in devices also show on the Topology in the OT view when an OT user clicks an access switch.

title: Topology: every device plugged into an access switch; OT editors get 🔌 Switch ports
items: Network map → Topology: click an access switch (focus view) and everything plugged into it is drawn below it on a bus — the Server Inventory devices of each port, else the name on the port — with the port number, an icon (camera, printer, access control, kiosk, TV, PLC, Moxa, gateway, sensor …) and OT devices in orange. Click one to open its port. Other switches show only the network devices as before.
OT editors now have 🔌 Switch ports on Server Inventory too: only the OT devices, on the Kabin switches the OT team sees; the devices to add are only the OT-looking ones and are saved as OT.

title: Server Inventory: 🔌 every device linked to its access-switch port; OT editors can add OT devices
items: New 🔌 Switch ports (IT admins) on Server Inventory: for every IT and OT device it finds the access-switch port it is cabled to on the network map — the map's device on that port (access points, card-reader switches …), its MAC or IP written on the port, or the same name — and writes it to "Connected to" (preview, tick what to apply). Devices behind a hub / Moxa keep the port the OT device list gave them.

It also lists what is on an access-switch port but has no Server Inventory record yet (printers, TVs, kiosks, Matrix readers, Moxa routers, gateways …) with a suggested name, IT / OT and category to add in one go — IP phones, PXE / spare ports and people's desk points are left out — and the records it could not find on any port (spares, or missing name / MAC / IP).
Network map: each switch port shows 📦 the Server Inventory devices connected to it (click to open the record); OT logins see the OT ones.
OT editors can now add OT devices too (+ Add Server → Add OT device): always saved as OT.

title: Server Inventory: OT editors can edit OT devices
items: OT team members with the Editor role can now edit the OT devices in Server Inventory (✏️ on the row, or Edit in the record) — IP, MAC, VLAN, OT system, connected switch port, location, serial, model, status, remark … Changes go to the record's History Usage; changing Serial / Brand-Model / Asset Code locks the record as for IT (an IT admin unlocks).
They cannot edit IT devices, add or delete records, or move a device from OT to IT. OT viewers still only look.

title: Server Inventory: OT devices — OT device list import, IT / OT filter, OT team view
items: New ⬆ OT device list button (IT admins) on Server Inventory: upload the CMDB list (e.g. CMDB_OEE.xlsx). The preview shows which Kabin switch each switch name of the file is (the file's names differ from the map's — e.g. "ASW-11" is the IT-KABIN11 switch; you can change any), the devices already on the map (found by MAC), the empty switch ports that will be filled (a port with several devices gets the Moxa / hub and lists the rest behind it), the ports where the map and the file differ (never overwritten) and data problems in the file. Apply adds the devices as OT records (category, IP, MAC, VLAN, OT system, connected switch port) and fills only empty fields of existing records. Uploading the same file again changes nothing.

Server Inventory has IT / OT now: an IT & OT / IT only / OT only filter, an OT badge, and IT / OT, MAC, VLAN, OT system and Connected to in the record. OT devices stay out of Needs Attention and Used / stock.
OT team logins see Server Inventory as "OT devices": only the OT records, read-only.

title: Network map: OT sees the factory cabinets; rack items no longer move by dragging
items: OT view: the 🗄 Racks tab shows every factory cabinet (IT-KABIN, CCTV-KABIN, HARICI KABIN) — never the server-room racks; the Drawings tab no longer lists the server-room rack pictures. Click a switch in a cabinet to open its ports.

Racks: dragging an item to another rack / U is switched off for everyone (no accidental moves). Click a device to see its ports; editors click a patch panel / PDU to edit it, where rack and U can still be changed.

title: Network map OT view: OT editors edit end-device ports, Drawings tab
items: OT editors (Users & Audit → team OT, role Editor) can edit the ports of their Kabin switches that go to end devices or are free: device name (camera, Matrix access control …), its port, cable, mode, VLAN, patch point, note, or disconnect. Ports cabled to a network device (AP, uplink switch) stay locked with "only IT can change this port", and an end-device port can't be cabled to a network device. OT viewers only look.
In the OT view, ports to APs and uplink switches stay green ("to network devices") even though OT does not see those devices.
OT now sees the 🖼 Drawings tab (rack pictures, factory / office plans with AP and cabinet pins, fibre routes) — view only.

title: Network map: OT view for the Operation Technology team
items: New team OT (Users & Audit → team "OT member"): OT logins see only the Network map, read-only, in its OT view — the Kabin switches (IT-KABIN, HARICI KABIN, CCTV …, card-reader switches) with every port and what is connected to them (cameras, Matrix access control, …), the core / distribution switches they uplink to (only those uplink ports), the VLANs in use there and their port changes. No Asset Inventory, racks, drawings, search or other pages; OT logins are always viewers.

IT team: an IT view / OT view switch next to the site lets you check exactly what OT sees. Each device has "OT team can see it?" (Automatic / Yes / No) in ✏️ Device, and switches shown to OT carry an OT badge in the list.
Server Inventory OT devices will follow when the data file is ready.

title: ♻ Stock & disposal: return → ready-to-reuse flow and disposal / write-off records
items: New button ♻ Stock & disposal on Asset Inventory. 🔄 Return → ready to reuse: a board of Stock assets — Returned → Wiped → Checked (condition grade A / B / C, optional photo) → Ready to reuse, with "Ready today" per asset type. A signed ↩ Return to Stock (or setting an Active asset to Stock) puts it in Returned; a ✍ Hand over takes it out.

🗑 Dispose / write off (IT admin, from the asset or a board card): sold / recycled / donated / scrapped / returned to vendor / lost — date, reason, data wiped (required for laptops, phones, tablets…), buyer / recycler, price and a certificate (PDF / photo). The asset goes to the Recycle Bin; the record keeps codes, cost center, cost and book value at disposal.
Disposals tab: list per year, 📊 Write-off list for Finance (.xlsx) and a SAP tick when Finance has written the asset off. Each step and disposal shows in the asset's 🕑 Timeline.

title: 🔍 Search everything (Ctrl+K), 👤 person view and 🕑 asset timeline
items: A search box in the top bar of every page (or press Ctrl+K): type a name, email, employee ID, serial, asset code, hostname, IP, MAC or switch-port name and jump straight to the asset, person, server, virtual server, network device, switch port or Intune device. You only see what you may open, in your countries.

👤 Person view (HR & IT): click a name in User Inventory or a person in the search — identity & AD (employee ID, AD department, last logon, manager), Microsoft 365 licence and last activity, their assets, Intune / Entra devices, signed handovers / returns, leaver checklist, My devices answers and changes, on one page.

🕑 Timeline in each asset's detail: bought, added, assigned, every change from History Usage, signed handovers / returns (with PDF), repairs, QR scans, photos, My devices answers and warranty end — newest first.

title: Asset Inventory: 📚 Models & warranty — tidy model names, auto Asset Type, fill warranty dates
items: New button 📚 Models & warranty (IT team) on Asset Inventory. 🧹 Clean-up groups the Brand/Model texts that are the same model typed in different ways (e.g. "Lenovo IdeaPad5", "Laptop Lenovo IdeaPad5-MP20T1R1" → "Lenovo IdeaPad 5"), with a suggested Asset Type. Tick, check, Apply: assets get the clean name (the old text, which often holds a serial or a person, is kept in Remark), empty Asset Types are filled and the model goes into the catalogue.
📚 Catalogue: one row per model with maker, Asset Type, warranty years and end-of-support year. New or edited assets with no Asset Type take the catalogue's type automatically.

🛡 Warranty: assets without a warranty date per maker, with the serial list (.txt / .xlsx) to check on the Lenovo / Dell / HP warranty site; upload the vendor's result file (.xlsx / .csv) to fill the dates (preview first), or estimate the rest from purchase date + the model's warranty years (marked "estimated" on the asset). Every change is written to History Usage.

title: Reports: our app vs Snipe-IT comparison (HTML)
items: New report in Reports → Overview: "Our app vs Snipe-IT" opens an HTML page comparing 38 features side by side (✔ / ◐ / ✘ with notes), with counts of where each is stronger, search and filters.

Also covers cost and running it (Snipe-IT is free AGPL-3.0 self-hosted or a paid hosted plan), a recommendation, and ideas worth borrowing (accessories / consumables, automatic Intune sync, email on handover, Microsoft single sign-on, kits). Print / save as PDF from the page.

title: User Inventory: AD department and cost-center department side by side, never mixed
items: The Department column shows two separate lines: AD — the department in the AD user list (e.g. Sales), and Cost center — the department that goes with the cost-center number (e.g. HV - Distributor - North Vietnam), with its ✏️ edit button. The cost-center number stays in its own column.
The AD upload never changes the cost-center department; search now also finds people by cost-center department or number.

title: AD user list: Department and Employee ID
items: Upload AD list now also reads the two new columns of the AD export: Department and Employee ID (an empty cell or "-" keeps what is already there, e.g. from the Entra user export). The preview says how many accounts have each.

User Inventory shows the Employee ID next to the name (ID 250032) and the AD department under the Department column (AD: Sales). The HR Department / Cost Center pair is not changed — the AD department names are a different list.
Search finds people by Employee ID, AD department and second email too; the User Inventory Excel export has Employee ID and AD Department columns.

title: Viewers no longer see Needs Attention
items: Users with the Viewer role do not see anything of ⚠️ Needs Attention (things to fix / to add): no menu link and no Needs Attention page, no missing-info / alert cards on the Dashboard, no 'Needs Info' counter and Needs Attention buttons in Asset Inventory, no Needs Attention button in Server Inventory, no 'status to check' part in 📦 Used / stock, no ⚠ check in the floor-plan popups, and no alert bell.
The lists themselves are also refused to viewers by the server. Admins and editors see everything as before.

title: Floor plans: office AP cables, labels that never overlap, jump between drawings · Server Inventory: Used / stock
items: Office K1 plan: the access points are cabled to the server room (racks MR-01…04, ground floor) and, upstairs, to the 1st-floor rack panel — where the office APs' switch (MR-01/ASW-05) is.
Pin labels never cover each other or another pin any more: a label that would overlap slides down, with a thin line to its pin (the IT + CCTV cabinet pairs are now readable).

Every drawing has Go to: buttons for the other drawings. A cabinet / AP that is also on another drawing shows 📄 buttons in its popup that open that drawing with the same pin selected (e.g. IT KABIN 7: site plan ⇄ factory plan).

Server Inventory → 📦 Used / stock: per model, how many records are in use according to the network mapping (a device of the map, or cabled on a switch port in the port sheets) and how many are stock, next to the quantity in the implementation document. Records whose status disagrees are listed (e.g. 'Active but not in the mapping' = a spare marked Active) with a button to set them to Stock / Active.

title: Site plan: fibre cables between cabinets, along their real routes
items: The site plan now shows every fibre cable along the route drawn in the CAD file: the outdoor ring (orange — e.g. SERVER ROOM → HARİCİ KABİN 1, 12C SM, 167 m; KABİN 1 → 2, 255 m …), the 48-core IT cables (blue) and 24-core CCTV cables (purple) from the server room to each factory cabinet. A SERVER ROOM pin marks where they all start.
Click a cabinet: its cables are highlighted with name · cores · length on the line, and listed in the popup — click the other end to jump there.
Access point popup: ⚠ when the AP is not in the map, has no switch port, or its name points to another cabinet than the one its switch is in.
Uploading a drawing package with the same name now replaces that drawing (pins and cables included).

title: Floor plans: AP → cabinet cables and an info popup on the plan
items: 🔌 Cables: each access point is joined to its cabinet with a line in the cabinet's colour — the AP name says which: K7-A5 = AP 5 of cabinet 7 → IT KABIN 7 (HK12-A1 → HARİCİ KABİN 12); if the name does not tell, the switch port it is cabled to in the map decides. Turn the lines on / off in the top bar.

Clicking an AP or a cabinet now opens a popup on the plan instead of leaving it. AP: device, model, IP, MAC, serial, the switch + port + VLAN it is on, and its cabinet. Cabinet: what is in it (with U), and the APs cabled to it — click any of them. The chosen pin's cables are highlighted, the rest fade. 🔷 Ports in the map / 🗄 Open in Racks are still there as buttons.

title: Network map: floor plans from the CAD drawing, with AP and cabinet pins
items: Network map → 🖼 Drawings → ⬆ Upload pictures now also takes a drawing package (.json: the picture with its pins). Three packages were made from the CAD file 18.1 TELEPHONE AND LAN SYSTEM: Factory (44 APs + 10 cabinets), Office K1 (15 APs, two floors) and Site (31 cabinets — outdoor HARİCİ KABİN 1–12, IT / CCTV cabinets — with the fibre routes and lengths).
Each pin sits on the AP / cabinet symbol of the drawing; click an AP pin to open that access point's ports, a cabinet pin to jump to its rack.

title: Server Inventory: Serial # column instead of OS
items: The server list shows the Serial # (where OS was) — handy for checking labels. The OS is still in each server's View details and in the search.

title: Virtual servers: Status column
items: New Status column with a coloured badge: Active (green), Powered off (grey), Maintenance (amber), Decommissioned (red). Change it in Edit (drop-down) and filter the list by status.
Powered-off and decommissioned servers are no longer flagged 'Not in the backup reports'. Long descriptions stay inside their cell (3 lines, hover for the full text).

title: Virtual servers: backup jobs from the daily backup report
items: Server Inventory → ☁ Virtual servers → ⬆ Import backup report: choose the 'Daily Backups Hayat Vietnam' e-mails (NetBackup OpsCenter) saved from Outlook as .msg — several at once is fine; .eml / .txt work too. The file is read in your browser; each backup job is kept as a record (job, server, policy, status, start, end, status code). Importing the same report again adds nothing twice.

New column Last backup: ✓ green with the time of the last job, amber if older than 2 days, red ✗ if it failed, plus the last whole-VM image backup and failed jobs in the last 7 days. Servers that never appear in a report show 'Not in the backup reports'.

🗄 Backups: every job by day, filter by server and period (1 day to 1 year), success / failure count. Names the backup software uses that are not a hostname (VxRail Manager, vCenter Server Appliance, vRealize Log Insight) are matched to VNHCMCESXMGMT / ESXVCSA / ESXLOG; any other unknown name (e.g. VNHCMCLPHYMMS01, VNHCMCLPHYRTG01) is listed so you can link it to a server or add it.

title: Network map: MAC address on every device
items: Every device has a MAC address field (✏️ Device), shown in the device panel and the hover tip; type it in any spelling (689e.0b8a.e378, 68-9E-…) — it is saved as 68:9E:0B:8A:E3:78. Search the map by MAC too.

Import Factory Info fills it from the workbook where the file has one: all 57 access points (AP list / equipment list) and the 3 Zebra label printers. The workbook has no MAC for the switches, firewalls, routers, WLCs or servers — add those by hand (e.g. from 'show version').
The third Zebra printer (VNF-BPro03, IP not given yet in the file) is now added too.

title: Network map: horizontal layout, groups in colour, the selected device shown in the racks
items: Topology → ↔ Horizontal: the layers run left → right (ISP, firewalls, core, distribution, servers, access switches, APs / printers) with a heading per column, sized to fill the screen; inside a column devices follow what they are cabled to, so fewer lines cross. ↕ Vertical brings back the saved layout. Your choice is remembered.

Each group has its own colour (list header, ring around the device on the map, outline in the racks). Click a group name in the list to show that group: its devices stand out and everything else fades — on the map, in the logical / physical / system views and in the racks. Click it again (or ✕) to show all.

Racks: the device you choose (in the list, on the map or in a rack) is outlined and blinks, its rack is framed in yellow, the page scrolls to it, and a line says where it is (e.g. MR-04 U10–11). The device panel has 🗄 Show where it is in the racks.
Fix: the racks are reloaded right after a Factory Info import.

title: Budget: Finance control (local SAP) vs Turkey report
items: Upload the Finance team's IT_Opex_Control_Table_<Mon><YY>.xlsb on the Budget page (sheet "SAP data", PIC = IT). The newest month is enough — it has every month so far, and Finance restates earlier months; older files are skipped.

New card Finance control vs Turkey report: Finance's own budget vs actual by local cost type (USD or VND), and a reconciliation with the Turkey B-F report by S4 GL and month (✓ same, Different, Only in Turkey report, Only in Finance).
Click a GL row to see Finance's SAP postings (date, document, cost center, text, VND, USD) next to the Turkey report lines for that GL.

title: Network map: import the Factory Info workbook (Palo Alto, APs, racks, VLANs, VMs, printers)
items: Network map → ⬆ Import Factory Info (.xlsx) (admins): the workbook is read in your browser and compared with the map, Server Inventory and the virtual-server list. You see every difference, grouped, and tick what to apply. Blank cells never clear what is already there.

Topology: the two Palo Alto PA-440 WAN firewalls (VNFCTPALWAN01 / 02, 10.84.8.252 / .253, MAIN RACK 04) are added with their links to ASW-06 / ASW-07. The old VFW-01 / VFW-02 nodes are marked Retired: they stay in their rack but are hidden from the topology. Any device can be set to Retired / In use in ✏️ Device.

Other link changes from the SWPORT sheets: the DD-6300 now uses its 10G ports to CSW-01 / CSW-02 (the copper ports are marked unplugged), the DSW uplinks to ASW-03 / ASW-04 are swapped, SR-07/ASW-11 is now a C9200L-48P, and there are 3 new card-reader switches and the Viettel VNTT line. Card readers, OT kiosks, Moxa gateways, printers and PXE ports appear in the port notes.
Access points: the 57 APs of the AP list become map devices, cabled to their switch port. Where the AP list and the port sheet name different ports, both are shown for you to choose (not ticked).
Racks are rebuilt from RACK LAYOUT with real U positions: MR-01 to MR-04 (including the CCTV switches and the ODF trays in MR-02) and all 35 factory cabinets with ODF, patch panel, switch and PDU.
VLAN tab: VLAN name, description and DHCP range, the new VLANs (131–133, ISP 600 / 601 / 35), VLANs used on ports but missing from the list (e.g. 134 PXE), and the devices whose IP is in each VLAN.

Server Inventory: hostname, IP, location and MAC / switch port are filled from the equipment list and the AP list (empty fields only — a different value is shown as a conflict to check, e.g. the two DSW serials). New tab ☁ Virtual servers: the 20 VMs and 4 ESXi hosts (linked to the VxRail nodes), with what each is for — editable.
Printers of the PRINTER sheet are on the map with their IP, location and print server. IP phones and the phone request list are not imported.

title: Budget import: older files can't overwrite newer data
items: Import now skips a country/year when the loaded data has more actual months (e.g. a 2025 mid-year file with actuals to April over a report with actuals to August, or a budget-only draft over a year with actuals). The preview shows the reason.
Files with two comment columns for the same year (mid-year + yearly explanation, e.g. TECH_66 Budget files) keep both comments.
The 2025 TECH_66 Budget files can add 2024 full-year actuals; their 2025 / 2026 parts are skipped because newer data is loaded.

title: Network map: the page stays still when you click a device
items: Clicking a device on the map, in the list or in a rack no longer scrolls the page down to the device panel — the topology stays in view; scroll down yourself to see the ports.

title: Needs Attention: named per group, servers on the Dashboard and the Needs Attention page
items: Each list now says what it is about: ⚠️ Needs Attention — Assets: Missing Info, — Assets: Missing AD & Asset, and — Servers & Network: Missing Info.

Dashboard: a new card with the number of servers / network devices that need info, split by issue (Serial, Hostname, IP, Location, Serial ≠ document) — Open the list → goes to the Needs Attention page.
Needs Attention page: the Servers & Network list sits under the asset lists, with the same fill-in-place inputs as in Server Inventory.

title: Server Inventory: Needs Attention — Missing Info
items: The 'Check vs document' button is replaced by ⚠️ Needs Attention — Missing Info (with a count), like on Asset Inventory.

It lists devices missing a Serial, Hostname, IP or Location (access points: Serial only), serials used twice, and serials that differ from the implementation document — fill them in right there and Save.
On top: whether every model matches the quantity in the document. Devices added after the document (Palo Alto PA-440) count as fine.

title: Budget: group by several fields, year-over-year item details
items: Budget lines: Group by is now on/off buttons — switch on 1 or more of PYP, Category and GL; lines are grouped by them in the order you click (e.g. ① PYP ② GL = each PYP split by GL) with subtotals at every level. No grouping = flat list.
The tick-box Combined selection is removed (replaced by the multi-level grouping).
Year over year: click a row ▸ to see the items behind it (program › project › sub-project, with PYP), each with its yearly amounts and ± change, biggest change first.

title: Server Inventory: check against the document · Nexus not grouped
items: Groups now hold only models with more than 4 devices (C9200L ×22, 3560-CX ×10, APs); models with 1–4 devices (the 2 + 2 Nexus switches) show as normal rows.

🧮 Check vs document: for every model the quantity in the document's equipment list, the devices in its port tables and the Server Inventory records (active / stock) — ✓ matches, ✗ missing or ＋ more. Today every model matches (Palo Alto PA-440 is not in this project).

Records to check: no serial, the same serial twice, a serial different from the document (e.g. the voice routers FDO2443M07Q vs FDO24410HDF in the document), or a device that is not in the document's port tables (spares) — with 👁 and ✏️ Add info to fix it there. Also listed: devices of the document whose serial is not in Server Inventory.

Import fix: importing the document again (replace) keeps the devices that are still in it — rack places, map positions and Server Inventory links are no longer lost; devices are linked to Server Inventory by hostname too. The equipment list (section 2) is now imported.

title: Budget: combine PYP / GL / Category, year-over-year changes
items: Budget lines: tick any PYP, GL or Category group (switch the grouping to mix them) — the Combined selection panel adds them up: CAPEX / OPEX / total, the 12 months and the lines. Untick or ✕ to remove; each line is counted once.
Year over year: (+) Changes vs last year adds a ± column after each year (budget vs last year's budget, actual+forecast vs last year's) with %.
Country flags now show on Windows too (they appeared as "VN").

title: Network map: floor plans with pins
items: 🖼 Drawings → click any picture (fiber layout, AP layouts of Production / Hygiene / Transformer / Office floors, topology, racks) to open it full screen with zoom.
📍 Edit pins (editors): click the picture to add a pin — 🗄 cabinet / rack, 📶 access point, 🔷 network device or 📝 note — drag to move, click to change or remove, then Save pins.
Click a cabinet pin to jump to that cabinet in the Racks tab; a device pin opens its ports. Each picture shows how many pins it has.

title: Network map: topology views like the document
items: Topology → choose the view: Layers (click a device to focus), Logical, Physical or System.

Logical (like 5.2): ISP lines → WAN firewall cluster → core pair (vPC) → server / distribution switches → 'EDGE SWITCHES: 16 PCS' (click to show them), VxRail / Data Domain on the left, WLCs on the right; IPs under every device, 1 G blue / 10 G green, port-channel labels (Po3001 …).
Physical (like 5.3): factory cabinets IT-KABIN2 … 12 on the left and racks MR-01 … MR-04 as boxes with their devices in rack order; cables CAT6 blue, fiber single-mode yellow, fiber multi-mode green.
System (like 5.1): core pair → server switches → VxRail nodes and Data Domain, with the port names at both ends of every link.

title: Budget Tracking redesigned: 2027 budgets, months, Opex/Capex, PYP
items: 2027 approved budgets for Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia can be loaded; the monthly B-F report adds 2025 and 2026 budget, actual (Jan–Aug), forecast (Sep–Dec) and comments.
Pick year, country and period (full year, YTD, quarter or one month); KPIs, Opex/Capex by country, a monthly grid and year-over-year comparison follow the filters.
Opex and Capex are shown separately; lines are grouped by PYP — switch between the new S4 code and the old ECC code.
Turkish names and comments are shown with their English translation next to them.
Click a line for all details, the 12 months and to add your own IT note; import shows a preview before saving.

title: Network map: real device panels, patch panels, cable path
items: Each device's ports are drawn where they are on the real hardware: Catalyst 9200L (48 ports in 4 groups, odd top / even bottom + 4 SFP+ uplinks), 3560-CX, Nexus 3524 / 3548 (SFP+ cages), ISR 4331, WLC 5520, R740xd and VxRail rear (iDRAC, built-in, PCIe card), Data Domain, Sophos XG 210. Green = to a network device, cyan = to a user / patch panel, grey = free; click a port to change it.
Patch panels from table 8.1 (MR01/PP01–PP10: D01–D105 data, T01–T105 phone): click a patch panel in the Racks tab, or an outlet (D07) in a port list, to see which switch port each outlet goes to.
🔎 Cable path in every port: wall outlet → patch panel port → switch port (VLAN) → uplink → distribution → core.
Import fix: "PORT 1 (LAN)" = "PORT 1" and "PORT 01" = "PORT 1" — no more duplicate ports on the OT firewall and WLCs (import the document again to apply).

title: Network map: Racks and Drawings
items: 🗄 Racks tab: the server room (MR-01 … MR-04, 42 U) and the factory cabinets (IT-KABIN2 … HARICI-KABIN12, 12 U) drawn from where each device is ('MAIN RACK - 03 (U29)'), with patch panels (MR01/PP01–PP10), cable managers and PDUs, and 'x / 42 U used' per rack.
Click a device in a rack to see its ports; editors drag items to another U or rack, add patch panels / PDUs / UPS / blanks, or add racks. Admins: ⚙ Build racks / Place new devices.
🖼 Drawings tab: upload the document's pictures (racks, topology, AP / floor plans, fiber layout) — tick 'Show the document's rack drawing' to compare with the live racks.

title: Server Inventory ← implementation document
items: Network map import now also reads the IP MGMT and System tables: every device gets its IP list (VxRail: iDRAC, vMotion, vSAN, ESXi; cluster VXR-MGMT, vCenter, PS), services (SSH, https 4444 …) and service tag — never user names or passwords.

Server Inventory → 🔄 Update from network map (admins): a preview that fills hostname, management IP, rack location (MAIN RACK - 03 (U29)), role / name and the IP list into each record, matched by serial / service tag.

Devices whose serial in the document differs from the record (or has none) are matched by model and shown with ⚠ and not ticked — pick the right record in the list. Devices missing from Server Inventory (the VNPT and Viettel lease-line routers) can be added.
🗺 next to a hostname opens the device on the network map; the network map shows its IP list and a link to the Server Inventory record.

title: Network map: click a device to see only what is cabled to it
items: Clicking a device now shows only that device and the devices cabled to it: ▲ in front (towards firewall / core) above, ▼ behind (towards access / servers) below, same layer left and right.
"2 steps" also shows the next devices along; "Show all" brings back the full map; "◎ Only …" goes back to the focused view. Click a neighbour to move the focus to it.

Import: the document's two spellings of the same switch (MR-01/ASW-01 and MR-01/DATA-ASW-01, T1/1/1 and T 1/1/1) are now joined, so the factory office switches show their uplinks — import the document again (Replace) to get them.

title: Network map · Server Inventory groups · device specs
items: New page Network map (menu, after Server Inventory): the site's topology like a Cisco lab — firewalls, routers, core / distribution / access switches, WLC, servers and storage in layers; orange = fiber / SFP, blue = copper, dashed = port-channel. Drag devices, zoom with the wheel, hover a link to see its ports.

Click a device: its front panel (green = to another network device, cyan = to users / patch panel, grey = free) and the full port list. Click any port to change what it connects to (device + port, cable, access / trunk, VLAN, port-channel, patch panel, note) — the other device's port is updated too. ⇄ Move swaps a cable to another port.

⬆ Import implementation doc (admins): the .docx is read in your browser — devices, switch-port assignments and the VLAN – IP table come in (the Vietnam factory document: 41 devices, 1,161 ports, 84 links, 23 VLANs). VLANs tab, Port changes history (who / when / before → after), ⬇ Export to Excel (CSV).
Server Inventory: categories with more than 4 devices (Access Point, Switch, Outdoor AP) are one line each — models and counts, click to open.
(i) next to every model: a popup with a drawing of the device and its main specifications (ports, throughput, PoE, capacity …) researched from vendor datasheets.

title: My devices: Active devices only
items: The confirmation page, the signed forms and the My devices report only list Active devices — Broken and Stock devices are kept by IT and are not asked.
User Inventory shows ○ not confirmed only for people who hold at least one Active device.

title: User Inventory: My devices status only
items: The Confirm button on each row is gone — use ✉ Ask everyone to confirm at the top.
Each person with devices shows a status: ✅ confirmed (click → signed forms), ⚠ N not with them, ⏳ waiting since … (link opened / sent, not confirmed), or ○ not confirmed.
IT admins can still click a not-confirmed status to see the details or make a personal link.

title: My devices open link: new link each time, old ones stop after 2 days
items: Every click on ✉ Make open link & message creates a new, different link.
Older open links of the same country (or all countries) stop 2 days later, so a link that was forwarded or posted somewhere cannot be used for long.
New links are open 2 days by default (max 14).
Admins and editors with Asset Inventory access can make open links (editors who only have User Inventory cannot); the personal 📨 link stays IT admin only.

title: My devices: one open link for everyone
items: User Inventory → ✉ Ask everyone to confirm (IT admin): make one link for all staff or one country, with a ready message — 📋 Copy it into one email or a Teams post.
Each person opens it, types their company email (…@hayat.com.tr or their second email), sees their devices and presses Confirm — no personal link needed.
Answers appear like the personal links: ✅ confirmed in User Inventory, the My devices report and the signed forms. The list shows how many confirmed per link; Stop ends a link.

Note: easier but weaker than the personal 📨 link — anyone who knows a colleague's email could open that colleague's list. Each answer keeps IP / browser; emails not in the list are limited to 10 per hour per network address.

title: My devices: signed Delivery form & Custody Agreement
items: User Inventory → click "✅ confirmed … 📄" (admins and editors) to open the signed forms of that confirmation.

🧾 Delivery-Acceptance form (VN.FR.07.01): every device the person answered "I have it" on one form, with the ✔ E-SIGNED stamp (email, time, IP, reference) in RECEIPT BY · Signature/Date — 👁 Preview / print / Save as PDF, or ⬇ the company Excel form filled in and signed.
📄 Custody Agreement (HQ) per device, with the same e-signature stamp under Received Party — preview, print or save as PDF.
Devices answered "Not with me" are listed apart and are not put on the forms. To send to the user: Save as PDF and attach it to an email.

title: AD list: second email (Email Address) · My devices accepts it
items: Upload AD list now reads the new "Email Address" column — each person's market email (…@hayat.vn, @molfix.co.th, @molped.com.my …) — and keeps it as a second email. It shows under the name in User Inventory (✉ …).
My devices: the page accepts either email — <AD name>@hayat.com.tr or the second email — and the person signs with the one they typed.
The ready message is addressed to both emails (Copy message / Open in Outlook) and tells the person they can use either.
Upload AD list ignores the empty "Modify User" rows some AD exports contain — they no longer show as shared / function accounts.

title: My devices: email = signature, phones & tablets
items: No more typing your name: the work email you checked on the page is the signature ("✍️ You sign with your work email …").
Phones & tablets from Intune now show on the page. Turkish staff (company phone / tablet) confirm them like their laptop (✓ I have it / ✗ Not with me).
Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia staff see them as "You are also signed in on these devices" — personal, nothing to confirm.
Turkish staff are recognised by name; IT can change it per person in the window (Automatic / Company phone-tablet / Personal).
User Inventory: the My devices button is now a clear blue ✉ Confirm button.

title: My devices report · User Inventory columns fixed
items: Reports → Lifecycle & audit → "My devices — confirmations" (HR & IT): Excel / PDF / HTML. Dashboard: people with devices, confirmed, waiting, not sent yet, devices "not with me" — per country and department, answers by month.
Sheets: People (state, links sent, opened / email checked / confirmed times, wrong emails, signed name), every Answer (time, IP, browser), and the devices people say are not with them.
User Inventory: the Last seen column is narrow again and the Assets column (count, 📨, confirmation status) stays on one line.

title: My devices: staff confirm their own devices
items: User Inventory → 📨 next to a person (IT admin): see their devices and earlier answers, then 📨 Make link & message — a ready email with a ✅ Check & confirm my devices button. 📋 Copy message and paste it into Outlook to that person (or ✉️ Open in Outlook / 🔗 Copy link only).
The personal link works 14 days; a new link replaces the old one. The page asks for the person's work email and shows the devices only when it matches our record — 5 wrong emails lock the link.
The person answers ✓ I have it / ✗ Not with me (with a note) for each device, can add a device that is missing from the list, types their name to sign and presses Confirm.
Each answer is recorded with time, IP and browser (Audit Log); "Not with me" or a missing device raises an IT alert. The Assets column shows ✅ confirmed / ⚠ not with them / 📨 sent with the date.

title: New label size: Big label 15 × 15 cm
items: Paper → "Big label · 15 × 15 cm" on the Stocktake page, the QR labels panel / page and the label preview — one label per page.
Large QR with the asset code, type · model, status, serial, PC No, place, department, holder and purchase date.
A broken laptop also gets a 🔩 spare-parts grid (each part ✓ usable / ✗ broken / ↪ used as spare / ? not checked), its condition, note and who checked it.

title: Small QR labels show the spare parts of broken laptops
items: On the A4 sheet and label-printer labels (63.5 × 38.1 mm), a broken laptop now has a parts strip under the QR: ✓ usable · ✗ broken (struck through) · ↪ used as spare · ? not checked, for Scr, MB, RAM, KB, Bat, SSD, Chg.
A Total broken laptop shows "✗ TOTAL BROKEN — no usable part". Marks print clearly in black & white too.

title: Stocktake: parts column for broken laptops
items: Each broken laptop line has a Parts column: one tag per part — Scr, MB, RAM, KB, Bat, SSD, Chg — green ✓ usable, red ✗ broken, blue ↪ used as spare, grey ? not checked (or ✗ Total broken). Hover a tag for the full name.
A legend shows above the list when it holds broken laptops; the column updates right after you save 🔩 Parts.

title: Broken laptops: Edit opens the spare parts
items: On Stocktake and QR labels, a broken laptop's button is now 🔩 Parts: it opens its spare-parts check (each part usable / broken / used as spare, Total broken, note) instead of the asset form.
Need to change the asset itself? Press ✏️ Edit asset info in that window.

title: Stocktake: more info, ✏️ Edit in place, collapsed models, QR labels panel
items: Each asset line now also shows the ECC code, holder and department, purchase date with age, warranty end, remark, and the 🔩 parts condition of broken laptops.

✏️ Edit on every line opens the asset right on the Stocktake page (status, site, holder, department, serial, model, purchase date, remark…) — save and print without leaving the page. Same rules as Asset Inventory: parts check when a laptop is set to Broken; IT admins can 🔓 unlock a locked holder there.
Model groups start closed — open only the model you need (or Expand / collapse all).
🏷 QR labels (top bar) and 🏷 All QR labels (in a stocktake) open the full labels list as a panel on the same page — no new page. ✏️ Edit is there too, and on the QR labels page.

title: Stocktake: lists by model, tick & print labels, click to preview
items: In a stocktake, every list (Not scanned yet, Found, Found elsewhere, outside filter) is grouped by model with a checkbox per asset and per model.
Pick the paper (tall 6.5 × 14 cm is chosen for Broken stocktakes) and press 🖨 Print labels (N) — only the ticked labels print.
Click an asset to preview its QR label, change the paper there, and 🖨 Print this label.

title: QR labels: list, tick & print, preview
items: The labels page lists every asset straight away, grouped by model (biggest first), with filters for country, site, asset type, status and search.
Tick assets — or a whole model with its group box — and press 🖨 Print selected (N).
Click an asset to preview its label in the chosen paper size, with a 🖨 Print this label button.
Admins see 🏷 printed / 📷 scanned counts on each row.

title: Tall QR label 6.5 × 14 cm with spare parts
items: QR labels → Paper: "Tall label · 6.5 × 14 cm" — one label per page with a big QR, code, type / model, status, serial, PC No, place, department, holder and purchase date.
A broken laptop's label also shows its 🔩 spare parts: condition and each part (✓ usable, ✗ broken, ↪ used as spare, ? not checked) with the parts note.
A stocktake of Broken assets opens its labels in this size.

title: Reports page: one line per report
items: Reports are listed one per line — name and description on the left, Excel / PDF / HTML on the right — grouped as before; team-only reports are tagged (IT & HR, IT, admins).

title: KPIs: data quality by asset type · 7 new reports
items: KPIs → Data quality is now a table by asset type × country, with what is missing (no serial / asset code / PC No – AD Name / duplicate serial).

New reports (Excel / PDF / HTML): KPIs, Depreciation & book value, Stocktakes (QR audit), Handover & return (e-signed), Leavers checklist, Microsoft 365 licence reclaim, and QR labels & scans log (admins).
Reports page: new groups Overview and Lifecycle & audit.

title: KPIs: utilisation by asset type
items: Utilisation is now a table: one row per asset type, one column per country — each cell is Active ÷ assets of that type, with counts and an Active / Stock / Broken bar. Types are never added together.

title: Stocktake: filters, print & scan log, photos
items: New stocktake: choose Status (Active / Broken / Stock), Asset type and Department as well as country / site; assets scanned at the place but outside the filter are listed separately.
Printing QR labels asks what for (first label, replacement, a stocktake, other) and records who printed and when; admins see on each label how often it was printed and scanned.
Every QR scan is recorded (who, when, from a stocktake or the phone camera, result).
Admins are asked for a photo after each scan — saved on the asset (shrunk on the phone); photos show in the asset detail and the scanned-label page.

title: Unlock in place (IT admin)
items: Return / Hand over window: a locked asset shows the lock at the top with a 🔓 Unlock button for IT admins — signature and note are kept, then Sign & save.
Edit Asset: "🔓 Unlock now" in the lock message makes User Name / AD Name editable right away (no trip to History Usage).

title: KPIs, Leavers, Stocktake with QR, e-signed handover, M365 reclaim, depreciation
items: 📈 KPIs: utilisation, ghost assets, data quality, repair time, leaver recovery and depreciation — split by country, with a monthly trend.
🚪 Leavers: return checklist per person (assets, Intune devices, M365 licence, AD account); assets tick themselves when returned with an e-signature; % returned within 7 days.
📷 Stocktake: print QR labels, scan with the phone camera — found / found elsewhere (Move here) / missing / unknown; closing a stocktake gives the ghost-asset KPI.
✍ Handover & return with e-signature (asset detail, Leavers, scanned label): the signed PDF is kept on the asset instead of the paper form.
♻ Licenses → Microsoft 365 reclaim: upload the admin centre Active users report; leavers still licensed and users with no activity for 60+ days, per country.
Book value on every asset (straight-line, 5 years — Circular 45/2013 allows 3–8 for IT equipment).

title: Users & Audit: page access of every account
items: 🔑 Logins has a new column with the pages each account can open — ✎ can change data, 👁 read only — and its countries, next to last login, so access can be reviewed any time.
Worked out from the same rules the server enforces (role, team, countries, Asset Inventory access).

title: Reports: interactive HTML version
items: New 🌐 HTML button on every report: opens an interactive page in a new tab.
Dashboard: switch country (All / Vietnam / Thailand / …) or click a country chip, sort any table by clicking a column, show % of row, hover the mix bars for numbers, hide a colour from the bars.
Data tabs: search all columns (matches highlighted), filter by country, sort, 50 / 100 / 500 rows per page, download what you see as CSV.
Save the page (Ctrl + S) to keep it — it works offline.

title: Reports: numbers split by country, like the Dashboard
items: Report dashboards (Excel and PDF) now show each key number with the split per country (VN · TH · MY · …), like the Dashboard tiles.
Tables have one row per country — Office / Factory under Vietnam — with Total, Active, Broken, Stock (or the right columns for each report), a Total row and a status-mix bar.
By-type tables show one column per country, so countries are never just added together.

title: Reports: Excel dashboard with charts + PDF
items: Every Excel report now opens on a Dashboard sheet: key numbers, summary tables and charts (real Excel charts you can edit); the raw data follows on the next sheets, with filters and a frozen header.
New 📄 PDF button on every report: the same dashboard with charts, ready to print or email.
Asset / User Inventory sync still works with the new files: the Dashboard sheet is ignored on upload.

title: Audit Log: every login and every action
items: Users & Audit now records logins, failed logins, logouts, password changes, every change, Excel downloads and page visits — each with the user's IP address.
New "Logins" table: last login, last activity and failed logins (7 days) of every account.
Audit Log: search, filter by user / action / dates, hide page visits, page through all entries, download as Excel.

title: Reports: new Excel exports for the new functions
items: Devices (Intune / Entra): every device of AD users with compliance, last check-in / sign-in and linked asset, plus a sheet of differences to check.
User activity (AD / Intune / Entra): AD account, last AD logon, Intune check-in, Entra sign-in, days since last seen, and who needs a check (HR & IT).
Broken & Stock + spare parts: broken / stock devices with each laptop's parts check, spare parts per model and in total.
System Health (IT): collectors, latest status of every check, history of status changes.
Reports page is now grouped: Inventory · Devices & users · Maintenance · IT.

title: Broken laptops: parts check from Asset Inventory
items: Asset Inventory: a broken laptop's status is clickable and opens the parts check; below it you see "check parts", "N parts usable" or "total broken".
Setting a laptop to Broken (Edit, or Add Asset) now asks for the parts check first: all parts start as Usable — just mark the broken ones (or tick Total broken). Cancel = the asset is not saved.

title: Asset Inventory by user: "broken" is not a person
items: Assets whose AD Name or User Name is just "broken", "missing", "none", "stock"… are no longer grouped together as one user: each goes to its real user, or to "No user assigned".
Each user's header is now one line: name, email, position, then assets · devices · AD logon · manager · to check.

title: Spare parts: broken checkbox, all parts per laptop, remark, popup
items: Each laptop shows all 7 parts; tick "broken" on a part to take it off the count (untick to count it again).
The asset's remark is shown next to it; clicking the asset opens a details popup on the page.

title: Spare parts: counted from every broken laptop, by model
items: Each broken laptop counts as 1 of each part unless marked broken / used or Total broken.
Screen, Keyboard, Mainboard, Battery are counted per model (fit the same model only); RAM, SSD, Charger are counted together (fit any laptop).

title: Alerts box moved to Needs Attention
items: The 🔔 Alerts list is no longer on Maintenance & Repairs; it is at the bottom of the ⚠️ Needs Attention page.

title: Maintenance: SSD / Storage and Charger in the parts check
items: Broken laptops' parts check and the spare parts list now also cover SSD / Storage and Charger.

title: Maintenance: Broken & Stock devices + spare parts
items: All Broken and Stock devices are listed on Maintenance & Repairs, with a summary chart (status & type, laptop condition, country).
Broken laptops get a parts check: Total broken, or Screen / Mainboard / RAM / Keyboard / Battery as usable, broken or used as spare.
Spare parts list: usable parts by part and model, with the laptop they come from; Use marks a part as taken.

title: User Inventory: Needs check chart + last seen from AD, Intune and Entra
items: A chart at the top shows the people to check (no activity anywhere 90+ days, no AD logon 90+ days, not in the AD list, never logged on) and by country. Click a bar to list them.
The Last seen column shows days since the last AD logon, Intune check-in and Entra sign-in together. Resource accounts are left out.

title: Needs Attention: summary chart
items: Both Needs Attention panels now start with a chart of everything to fix — by what's missing, by country and by asset type. Click a bar to list those assets.

title: Devices: Needs check summary chart
items: A chart at the top shows everything that needs a check — by difference type and by country — for all devices, whatever the list filters.
The tiles also always count all devices; filters only change the list. Click a bar or tile to list those devices.
Asset Inventory by user: each user is now a separate block.

title: Bug fixes after a full review
items: Needs Info tile = Needs Attention list; tiles clear the Laptop filter; one person no longer split in View by user; sort works there.
Device Check links the right asset when Computer Nos repeat; merge respects locks; fewer false differences.
Country limits enforced on device actions, search and uploads; safer display of names (O'Brien etc. work).

title: Devices: compliance filter fixed
items: "Not compliant" / "Compliant" filters and tiles now use the same status as the Compliance column (Intune first, else Entra).

title: Asset Inventory: position next to each user
items: The user's Position and department (from User Inventory) are shown next to the name and email in View: by user.

title: Search shows Intune devices + SAP description mismatches
items: Asset Inventory search also lists matching Intune / Entra devices and who uses them.
Rows found only through the SAP asset description say so.
Device Check flags SAP descriptions naming another laptop's serial.

title: Merge puts the system first
items: Merging duplicates now takes PC No + Serial from Intune, User Name / AD Name from AD, and Brand / Model, Type, Location, Status from the record created from Intune.
SAP codes, department, cost center, purchase date and history stay from the old record.

title: Device Check: merge duplicate assets
items: Same serial on two assets (typos like O/0 included) and at most one with an SAP code → Merge: keeps the SAP record with the Intune Computer No + Serial, the other goes to the Recycle Bin.
Same serial on two SAP assets → flagged to check by hand, never merged.

title: Asset Inventory: view by user
items: Assets grouped by person, with each asset's Intune status and the person's other devices (PCs not in Asset Inventory highlighted, phones / tablets).
Switch back any time: View: list.

title: Device Check: Intune + Entra vs Asset Inventory (IT)
items: Devices → ⬆ Upload Intune + Entra: only devices of people in the AD list; nothing in Asset / User Inventory changes by itself.
Differences are highlighted (not in Asset Inventory, serial, PC No, user, brand) with Use Intune value / Mark as checked.
Compliance, company / personal, managed by, and days since the last check-in / sign-in.

title: AD upload: resource accounts are kept
items: Shared mailboxes / email groups (OU …/Resources) are now added to User Inventory too, marked Resource.
New filter: AD: resource accounts.

title: User Inventory: Last logon column
items: "Last updated" replaced by Last logon: date + days since (amber after 30 days, red after 90, "never" if the account never logged on).
New sort: longest since last logon first.
The AD account is shown in bold in the email (e.g. abilgili@hayat.com.tr), with the manager underneath.

title: User Inventory: upload the AD user list (IT admin)
items: ⬆ Upload AD list: preview first, then apply — matches people by AD account / email / name, adds new people, merges doubles, skips resource accounts (shared mailboxes, groups).
Each person shows their AD account, manager and last logon (red after 90 days).
New filters: Not in latest AD list · AD: no logon for 90+ days · AD: never logged on.

title: New: System Health page (IT)
items: Live status of routers, switches, servers and internal web apps, refreshed every 30 seconds.
First system: the DrayTek router — up time, WAN 1 / 2 / 4G backup up or down, live traffic.
IT gets an alert when something goes down or an office stops reporting.

title: Location & Operations and User Inventory tiles: evenly spread
items: The small figures under each tile are chips spread evenly across the tile (like Justify in Word): label on the left, number on the right.

title: Smaller summary tiles
items: Number and country split on one line — Dashboard, Asset Inventory and User Inventory tiles take about half the height.

title: "New app function update" box on the Dashboard
items: See what was deployed lately, newest first.

title: Asset & User Inventory: new summary tiles
items: Same style as the Dashboard: big number + split by country.
Click a tile or a country chip to filter the list (Needs Info opens Needs Attention for that country).

title: Custody Agreement prints on one A4 page
items: No more second page when printing.

title: User Inventory fits the screen
items: Email shows under the name, Devices column removed — all columns visible without scrolling sideways.

title: Lists show the latest changes first
items: Asset Inventory and User Inventory are sorted by last updated, with a Last updated column and New / Edited tags.

title: Devices page (Intune & Entra) — IT admin
items: Microsoft device list linked to assets and users.
Bulk import is paused for now; the first import was undone.

title: Users can manage one or more countries
items: Viewer / Editor / Admin can be global (all countries) or limited to the countries they manage.

title: Custody Agreement (HQ form)
items: New 🖨️ button in asset details prints the HQ custody form, incl. Asset No (S/4).

title: Needs Attention: fix missing info on the spot
items: Split by country, edit directly in the list — no need to open each asset.
Missing AD Name / PC No only checked for laptops and desktops.

title: Dashboard redesign
items: Totals split by country and status, Assets by Country / Type, Vietnam Office & Factory.
Top Models and Alerts side by side; Alerts is a pop-up button on the inventory pages.

title: Asset Inventory improvements
items: Years in Use column (from purchase date), Asset Type filter, Office / Factory filter.
Laptops, desktops and phones listed first; "Code" renamed to "Asset code".
